name: T1053.007
desc: Container Orchestration Job (T1053.007) — a runtime-compromised DaemonSet-owned Pod (container-orchestration scheduling primitive) is flagged; controller-stop+kinds (== native ActionRotate with the owner-eligibility gate widened to accept apps/v1 DaemonSet) evicts it and the owning DaemonSet respawns a clean new-UID Pod

fixture.requirement: The ControllerStopKindsFamily adapter (phvx-attack.py) AUTO-PROVISIONS this fixture in setup(): a fresh, uniquely-named demo-api clone (nginx+exporter behind a Service, steady load, PodMonitor, PhorvexPolicy enabled:[rotate]) OWNED BY A DAEMONSET, pinned to 2 least-loaded CriticalAddonsOnly IP-headroom nodes (exactly 2 Pods), minAvailableReplicas=1. It is torn down on teardown. A fresh uniquely-named workload per fire makes every fire a pristine FIRST rotate (a 2nd rotate on the same DaemonSet workload prices <=0 and no-ops, persisting via the manager audit replay). Manual equivalent: ~/phvx-farm/lane-csk-fixture.sh 7 ds-orch 2.
fixture.why_two_pods: availabilityFloor (internal/feasibility/defaults.go) refuses a rotate unless readyReplicas-1 >= minAvailableReplicas, and minAvailableReplicas DEFAULTS to 1 (api/v1alpha1 defaults.go EffectiveMinAvailableReplicas: 0 is treated as unset). So a single-replica DaemonSet (ready-1=0 < 1) is structurally INFEASIBLE to rotate; the workload MUST have >= 2 Ready pods. Empirically confirmed on lane p7: a 1-pod DaemonSet tick showed selected:0 infeasible:1. Two pods also yield a real sibling -> genuine two-sidedness.
fixture.why_coverage_clone: the brain only prices a POSITIVE-gain reactive rotate when the target carries a real protectable profile (Service graph + measured load + covered facts); an isolated bare pod gets no reactive decision (gain<=0 -> noop, suppressed by OnlySelected).

arm.note: Arm = inject a TRUSTED SecurityEvent (rule.source=p7-attacks, type=phorvex.attack.orchestration, threatLevel=critical, webhook-stamped phorvex.ai/creator-identity=system:serviceaccount:p7:p7-attacks) targeting the oldest Ready DaemonSet pod of the auto-provisioned workload. No image/config drift — the ONLY difference from a demo-api rotate is the owner kind (DaemonSet). Rotate is feasible ONLY because ownership.Check (csk build) accepts the DaemonSet owner (owner-kind-unsupported without the +kinds extension).

oracle.pass: A NEW manager decision row action==rotate selected==true feasible==true actuated==true dispatchOutcome==emitted on the TARGET DaemonSet pod, not in the pre-fire baseline (baseline_target_rows==0); AND the target pod-UID is evicted and replaced by a fresh-UID pod (clean DaemonSet respawn, oracle target_present:false then ready back); AND the sibling DaemonSet pod-UID stays intact (two-sided); AND availability holds (ready >= min_available).
